answer: In this PoA design, bonded escrows make correlated equivocation costly: if k identities coordinate on conflicting attestations, their penalty grows as P(k)=p·k², rather than as k independent small fines. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation, applying an exponential capital-loss multiplier such as r^k, with r>1. Thus a sybil swarm cannot treat a haven, gale, or juniper of aliases as cheap redundancy; shared control magnifies the collateral at risk.
